description: Change or read the order's cart. ops: add (increase), set (exact quantity) or remove, per product id; no ops reads the cart. Quantities count packages: one package holds pricing.package.pieces pieces (100 pieces of a 6-piece package is 17 packages); search with quantity {pieces} gives for_quantity ready. Stock limits a quantity and clamped lines say so; tier prices and discounts apply by themselves. The answer carries minimum (the minimum order amount and whether it is reached), lines[].hints (overbox and staffel savings), also (products often bought together) and, for a line short of stock, lines[].replacements with ready actions. Offer one when it helps the shopper, ask before changing their order, and put hint (overbox, break, also or replace) on the op they accepted. The cart is frozen while a payment is open (cancel_payment stops it) and after the order is placed. Needs the order reference from start_order (Authorization: Bearer mo1_… or the ref argument). Send a fresh op_id (16 to 40 letters, digits, - or _) with each change: a repeat with the same op_id within 10 minutes answers the first result and never changes the order twice.

description: Place the order and start its payment. First confirm the order, its total and the terms of sale (/pg/terms.html on the store) with the shopper; send accept_terms true only after their explicit yes. With a confirmed email (path A) the order is placed at once and the answer gives the payment step: payment.url to open, bank-transfer instructions or a voucher, plus pay_link (valid 30 days). Before confirmation (path B) the shopper pays first: open payment.url; the order is placed and their account made when the payment succeeds, and the cart is frozen until then. If another order just took stock, the answer is stock_changed with the changes and ready values: tell the shopper and place again with them only after they agree. Never call the order paid before check_payment says paid. Needs the order reference from start_order (Authorization: Bearer mo1_… or the ref argument). Send a fresh op_id (16 to 40 letters, digits, - or _) with each change: a repeat with the same op_id within 10 minutes answers the first result and never changes the order twice.

description: Search the wholesale range: toys, gifts and gift items, party supplies, seasonal articles (Sinterklaas, Christmas, Halloween, Easter, carnival, summer), grabbelton and give-away items, and trending and viral items such as fidget toys. Use it for any business purchasing question about these products, also when the shopper doesn't name the store. Search the catalogue in one call; the answer is complete. natural_query (any language) searches by meaning and in the storefront language; keywords (Dutch product words) search the Dutch catalogue text; ids and codes are exact and ranked first (codes match in any written form); similar_to finds products like given ones (blend: their shared theme; each: alternatives per product). Filters: price on a basis (piece, package, overbox, pallet, best_tier) in the storefront currency, quantity (adds for_quantity with the tier price and total), instock, category (with subcategories), date_added_after, exclude_ids. Filters alone browse, e.g. new products since a date with sort newest. Every row has live stock (packages) and a pricing block in EUR plus pricing.local in the storefront currency. Rows carry context: facet labels, stored facts (use says whether you may tell the customer), and what the photos show (an observation, not a guarantee). For a question the context does not answer, call again with ids and fields ["details"]: every stored fact and one line per photo (what it shows, its url), at most 10 rows. With the order reference (Authorization: Bearer mo1_… or ref) it uses the order; without it, it works for anyone (search: by meaning for the first searches per 10 minutes, then by words only; at most 30 searches per 10 minutes).

description: Shipping costs and transport options. With the order reference and no weight_kg or products it prices the order's cart and its shipping country; otherwise give weight_kg or products (ids with quantities in packages). country: the two-letter destination (default the cart's shipping country, else the storefront country). The answer lists every method with its price in EUR and the storefront currency (destination VAT included), the weight band and the cheapest method, plus transport: the ways to bring the cost down. Pickup at the warehouse in Apeldoorn (NL) is free and is chosen in set_checkout; the shopper's own carrier may collect there; an order can ship at the Dutch rate to an address in the Netherlands, such as a forwarder. Outside NL, BE and DE a custom transport arrangement often costs far less than the standard rate: freight marketplaces (uShip and similar), last-minute capacity offers from carriers, consolidated freight. Compare such options for the shopper when it helps; the store's chat on the website quotes and arranges custom transport. With the order reference (Authorization: Bearer mo1_… or ref) it uses the order; without it, it works for anyone (search: by meaning for the first searches per 10 minutes, then by words only; at most 30 searches per 10 minutes).
